title: Pristine Painting Restoration Alternative: Decks & Wood
description: Comparing Pristine Painting Restoration with Precision Paint Experts for a deck or wood restoration? Questions to ask about rot, cleaning, and stain choice.
h1: Pristine Painting Restoration vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Restoring a gray, splintered deck is a different job from painting a wall. Below is a plain checklist for weighing one wood restoration proposal against another, whoever wrote it.

questions: How do I know if my deck needs repair before staining?
Is stain or paint better for a Florida deck?

sections.h2: What restoration means on exterior wood
body: If Pristine Painting Restoration and Precision Paint Experts are both on your shortlist for a deck or porch, this page will not size up the other firm; we leave that to you. This page is about decks, porch floors, pergolas, and other exterior wood, where the word restoration should translate into specific steps on a written scope.

Months of UV, afternoon storms, and sticky air chew away the top layer of grain, split checks open along each board, and let rainwater soak into end cuts where decay gets its start. A coat of stain over that without repair and cleaning usually looks good for a season and then fades or flakes.

Restoration can also mean returning gray, weathered boards to something closer to their natural tone before a new finish goes on. Whether a silvered board can come back depends on how deep the weathering goes, so be wary of anyone promising a specific color before kneeling down and inspecting it. Gates, pergolas, and fence runs usually deserve the same cleaning and stain as the deck; finishing them in one visit keeps the whole backyard reading as one tone. For a sense of how far gone a fence can be and still recover, read our piece on bringing back a sun-damaged wood fence.

sections.h2: Check the boards before you compare bids
body: Walk the deck yourself first. Note any spongy wood around screws, blackened board ends, or planks with a bounce in them. The warning signs are laid out in our guide to spotting deck rot early. A contractor's estimate should then say whether rotted pieces will be replaced, and how that is approved.

sections.h2: Questions for any deck or wood restoration bid
body: Have each bidder put these answers on paper:
bullets: What cleaning method strips the gray, and what kills the mildew?
If a joist cap, board, or fascia is rotten, who signs off on swapping it and when?
Does the product soak into the grain, or build a film on top?
Which surfaces are included: deck floor, railings, stairs, skirting?
How long must the wood dry before the finish goes on?

sections.h2: How Precision Paint Experts restores wood
body: A crew lead, not a salesperson, kneels on your boards with a moisture meter wherever something looks off and photographs what is there. Soft washing, mildew kill, sanding, and swapping rotten pieces each get a separate line in the written scope. Bare decking and rails are finished with penetrating stains that wick down into the wood, while any railing you want painted is coated in waterborne urethane enamel.
More detail lives on our deck and fence stain service page and our wood staining and finishing overview. For homes near Gainesville, see deck staining in Gainesville.

Stain color is chosen with samples on your actual boards when possible, since the same stain can look very different on new pine and on aged wood. Your written quote spells out the stain brand and the number of coats we plan to apply.

Wood takes stain best in the cooler, drier stretch from October through May. In summer we start at first light and keep one eye on the dew point and the radar so a pop-up storm does not land on wet stain. Any extra board or added rail needs your signature before it is billed, a flaw spotted on the closing walkthrough gets corrected before we pack up, and outdoor jobs come with a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years. Ready to have someone look at the boards? Book a free deck estimate.

faqs.q: Will you swap out soft or rotten boards, or just stain over them?
faqs.a: We replace them. Any board or trim piece with rot is listed on the written scope you approve, so it is handled before a drop of stain goes down.

faqs.q: Which products go on the deck itself?
faqs.a: Walking surfaces and bare rails get a penetrating stain that sinks into the grain. If you prefer painted balusters or handrails, those receive a hard waterborne urethane enamel.

faqs.q: Can a deck be stained in the summer?
faqs.a: It can. Crews begin early, track the dew point, and check radar through the day. Fall through spring, roughly October to May, is still the more forgiving window for wood.
